questions.prompt: What should the standalone runner be?
questions.description: This decides where the tool lives and what layer it is responsible for testing.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Build a standalone OpenTUI app in this repo, separate from the new React frontend. It should be a developer test runner that spawns the real Plannotator command, writes realistic stdin, captures stdout/stderr, and observes the daemon.

questions.prompt: Which scenarios should be in scope for the first useful runner?
questions.description: These are fixture-backed simulations, not calls to live external agent products.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Cover every supported local protocol path with fixtures: Claude plan hook, OpenCode plugin plan/review/annotate/archive, Pi plugin plan/review/annotate/archive, Codex plan hook, Copilot plan hook, Gemini plan-file hook, and direct CLI review/annotate/archive. Network-heavy PR review should use local fixture data by default.

questions.prompt: How far should each scenario run automatically?
questions.description: This defines whether the runner only proves session creation or also proves stdout result completion.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Run through the full local process loop when possible: spawn command, detect session-ready stderr, verify daemon session appears, complete the session by POSTing to the real session API, then assert stdout/stderr/final exit behavior. Keep browser interaction manual or optional; do not require Playwright browser automation in this goal.

questions.prompt: Should the daemon expose a single event stream for the runner and frontend dashboard?
questions.description: The frontend currently loads status/session data through request/response APIs. A daemon-wide SSE stream would make session creation, status changes, and debug events visible live.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add a focused daemon SSE endpoint for integration visibility, with simple event types for daemon status, session created/updated/removed, and runner/debug notices where appropriate. The frontend test dashboard should subscribe to it and fall back to polling existing endpoints if unavailable.

questions.prompt: What should the frontend shell show for this goal?
questions.description: This is not the final Plannotator UI migration; it is a debug surface to prove the daemon/frontend connection while the OpenTUI runner drives scenarios.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add lightweight debug dashboard components to the new frontend shell that render daemon status JSON, active sessions JSON, selected session bootstrap JSON, recent daemon events, probe results for key per-mode APIs, and links to session URLs. Do not put the runner controls in the browser frontend.

questions.prompt: What should stay out of scope?
questions.description: This keeps the runner useful without turning it into a second product.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep out of scope: migrating the real plan/review/annotate/archive UIs, adding a browser-based simulator, depending on live external agent products, requiring network PR URLs by default, and adding advanced security/auth work beyond the repo's current local daemon posture.
